Q: Integrating Windows Explorer as a control in Windows 11 A: 
Imagine this:

You have a book inside a backpack.

You want to make the backpack bigger.

But instead you keep trying to resize the book.

That won’t work.

Because the book is inside the backpack.

Same idea here.

Windows Terminal (big window)
      ↓
PowerShell (running inside it)

In Windows 11, PowerShell often runs inside Windows Terminal instead of its own console window. Because of this, resizing the PowerShell process won't change the window size, since the actual window belongs to Windows Terminal.

To resize the window, you need to target the Windows Terminal process instead of PowerShell. PowerShell is just running inside a tab, so the window handle you're trying to modify belongs to Windows Terminal, not the PowerShell process. WindowsTerminal.exe

Q: Representing 128-bit numbers in C++ A:

Check out the cppalliance/int128 library that was released in 2025.

Boost.Int128 is a portable implementation of a signed, and an unsigned 128-bit integer and related functionality (e.g. bit counting). Importantly, on all platforms, the sizeof the types provided in this library are 128-bits.

The library is header-only, has no dependencies, and requires only C++14.

Q: AWS client VPN not connecting A:

This error usually means the Google authentication app is not fully configured for that user, not that the AWS VPN itself is broken. AWS is sending the user to Google to sign in, and Google is rejecting it.

I would check whether the Google app is still in testing, whether the affected user is added as an allowed test user, and whether the redirect/callback URL in Google matches the one AWS expects. I would also make sure the user is signing in with the correct Google Workspace account and that the app is allowed for that domain.

Q: Failed to load https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token A:

When you register your app, you must setup the Redirect URI/URL, usually this url will be added to the CORS header.
